questions.a: 'had started' — the starting precedes the arriving. A wrong answer 'started' makes both simultaneous — 'when + arrived' forces ordering.

questions.q: Fix: 'I had gone to the market and bought vegetables.'
questions.a: 'I went to the market and bought vegetables' — both events form one past sequence told in order; no flashback needed. 'Had' alone with no earlier-vs-later contrast is an error.
'had ended' — 'before' explicitly orders the events; earlier event → past perfect. A wrong answer 'ended' erases the two-event structure.

What is Past perfect? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Past perfect is the earlier-past: 'When I reached the station, the train HAD LEFT' — two past events, and 'had' marks which came first.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Past perfect?
questions.a: Students put 'had' on the wrong event (the later one) or use it for single past actions where no ordering exists ('I had gone to school' — alone, no second event, the 'had' is a mistake).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student orders two past events correctly — earlier event in past perfect (had + V3), later event in simple past — with when/after/before/by-the-time triggers.
